message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

* runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**  
* has an **RTX A6000** GPU attached  
* uses a standard machine type (e.g., `n1-standard-8`) – you can adjust the CPU/memory count as needed  
* is created in a specific zone (replace `us-central1-a` with your preferred zone)  
* is owned by a specific project (replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual GCP project ID)

> **NOTE**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services.  
> * The RTX A6000 is available only in certain zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`).  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled and a **service account** with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent) to run the commands below.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣ Set your project
export PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# 2️⃣ Choose a zone that supports RTX A6000 GPUs
export ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 3️⃣ Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom startup script
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --reservation-affinity=any \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### Optional: Custom Startup Script

If you want to install NVIDIA drivers automatically, create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
# Reboot to activate driver (optional)
# sudo reboot
```

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

**POST URL**

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
```

**Headers**

```
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` and `<YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>` with your actual project ID and OAuth 2.0 bearer token (you can obtain one via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`).

---

## 3. Quick Checklist

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Enable Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| 2 | Ensure you have a service account with `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` |
| 3 | Verify the zone supports RTX A6000 (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:us-central1-a"`) |
| 4 | Run the `gcloud` command or POST the JSON payload |
| 5 | (Optional) Verify GPU installation: `nvidia-smi` after SSH into the instance |

---

### Troubleshooting Tips

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Instance creation fails with “GPU type not found” | Wrong zone or GPU type name | Double‑check the zone and use `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| `nvidia-smi` shows no GPU | Driver not installed | Add a startup script that installs the NVIDIA driver |
| Billing error: “Quota exceeded” | GPU quota reached | Request a quota increase in the Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Quotas |

That’s all! Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and start using the RTX A6000 GPU for your workloads. Happy computing!
